Logitech M325 Wireless Optical Mouse with Designed-for-Web Scrolling - Freespirit 910-004160 I haven't used many wireless mice -- I've almost always just used the track pad on my laptop and was fine with that. But I've been having some problems with the track pad locking up on my new (Mar 2015) MacBook, so I went shopping for a wireless mouse.

Clearly, this Logitech M325 model is popular -- hundreds of reviews, most of them good -- and the price is certainly reasonable (depending on the seller and color/print, prices are within a few dollars of each other).

So, I ended up ordering this "Freespirit" model -- sleek black with a multi-color "splash" design -- primarily because I like the colors and the overall look of it.

I'm not disappointed. In fact, I'm more impressed than I thought I would be.

It performs just fine. I don't have a lot of room -- I use my laptop most fo the time on a small rolling stand with just enough room for the computer plus a beverage and a few pens in a pencil cup. No problem -- this thing works on a pad of paper, my leg, on the sofa seat beside me, etc. I wish the scrolling wheel operated a bit more smoothly, but it's not enough of a problem to warrant any drop in star rating.

The color was a bit of a surprise, too -- the "splashes" are metallic/pearlized, so they really shine against the black background.

Overall, I like this more than I thought I would. I've been using it for about 10 days, and I've noticed no problems at all. I'll definitely update this review if I notice any issues in the future. But so far, I REALLY like it. It's making my life a lot simpler, for sure.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker I've been relying on a cordless phone system with built-in call blocking, but it only stores 30 numbers. That gets filled up in short order, and I delete them and start over. I needed something better.

And this is definitely better. I'm using it with a cable-provided phone line and cordless phone system. And it works. Mostly.

The cool thing about this system is it intercepts everything by default, and announces that if the caller is a telemarketer, to remove us from their call list. It also announces that the caller can press "0" for the call to go through. This eliminates all robocalls, and most other unsolicited calls.

After the phone number is in the device's caller ID memory, you can then whitelist or blacklist it if you choose. Whitelisted numbers go straight through without an announcement and ring the phone normally. Blacklisted numbers are simply blocked. You might hear a partial ring, but that's the end of it.

There are a couple of down sides. When a caller presses "0", only the ringer in the device itself rings. It does not ring the phone system. If you're not near the room where the device is, chances are you won't hear it. So if you're expecting important calls, it's probably best to set the device to "off" when you're not within earshot of it.

And the other is -- and this may be a fault in the particular unit I received -- the "off" position is not always reliable. More than once it has continued to block calls when set to "off." If a really important call is expected, I'll probably just disconnect the unit from the phone system completely.

Other than that, it's effective. It blocks unwanted calls.
text_fidelity_b: SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker

Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black REVISED to 4 Star review: After using the antenna a week, I re-ran the channel search--which I should have done after installing it. I am able to pick up 38 of the 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my house. They all come in very clearly. The amplifier wasn't working at all, and we determined that the brick was defective. Plugging it into another USB brick didn't really improve the signal by much, but it at least worked.

All-in-all, I'm glad I bought it. I'm able to clearly receive: 4 PBS stations; 3 CBS stations; 1 each NBC and ABC; plus FOX, CW, and an assortment of crap (TCT, HSN, QVC) networks. Enough to make me happy to leave TWC and in the dust.

UPDATE: 8/2/2016 What I have found is that the signals from channels with transmitters within 10 miles are not being up, while those 12 miles and beyond are coming in clearly. I suspect this is due to my location and not the antenna. Still, the amplifier causes the entire thing to not work, so I don't know what's up with that thing.

This antenna arrived as indicated. However, instead of the nearly 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my home, I'm only able to get about 15. I installed it on the roof, and the direction did not seem to make a difference. NOTES:

Originally, I hooked this up and leaned it against the back of the TV before I had someone install it. I got no more channels installing it on the roof than I did that way.

The amplifier which comes in the box with this antenna actually made the signal worse--not better, so I disconnected that.

Give the few number of channels that actually come through, on hindsight, I would have bought a much cheaper antenna. It does not pull in channels more than about 20 miles away. Even channels 20 miles away aren't received.

Otherwise, the reception on the channels that do come through is great.

All of this may be because I am in an old, downtown neighborhood, with close houses and lots of trees. Although I installed it in an area of the roof free of trees.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black

I like the feel of the keys on this keyboard - the rubbery surface is nice; the bumps on the F, J and 5 keys are easy to feel. The lighted keys look very cool in the dark, and have a good, solid feel when I press them.

What I don't like:

~ The lights in the keys are too dim. You can barely see them in a lit room. There should be a way to adjust the brightness of these lights.

~ The Num Lock, Cap Lock, etc. lights are too bright. There should be a way to adjust these also.

~ The Keyboard sits at too low an angle for my taste - the back feet of the keyboard should be raised higher.

~ The smooth finish of the area around the keys shows fingerprints horribly. This surface should be matte.

All in all, I like the keyboard (and will keep it), I just wish that a few things about it were designed differently...
text_fidelity_b: Razer Lycosa Mirror Gaming Keyboard - Special Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Dual-Band Wireless-N600 Gigabit Router (RT-N56U) This router is very good in terms of speed and signal strength, it is better than the Cisco E4200 v.1. However I was also interested in the ability to backup to USB attached drives. The E4200 does a much better job, actually the RT-N56U fails miserably when trying to backup using Windows backup to a USB drive (NTFS or FAT32). It seems they do not have plans to make this work in the future.

Unfortunately their customer service do not offer too much help.

Following you will find how they answered a question I submitted regarding the USB attached drives issue:

My question:
I have been trying to use Windows Backup with a drive attached via USB to this unit. I
have tried different hard drives formatted both as FAT32 and NTFS. Backups always
fail. Mostly with Error code: 0x80070008. Is there a compatibility issue between this
router and Windows Backup? I still have two weeks to return this router if I cannot
make it work.

Their response:
The router has its own settings that will operate reguardless if the computer works or not. The computer has nothing to do with the router software one way or the other. If you need to back up the router setting then I suggest you take screen shots of the router to verify that you can save the settings from there.
Thanks Aaron Asus Support Team

Well, I am still trying to figure out what their response means...

Do not get this router if you need USB features. They do not work.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Dual-Band Wireless-N600 Gigabit Router (RT-N56U)

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black I run during the summer and run outside. I hate carrying heavy items with me, like water bottles and phones. I feel they sort of hinder my performance, though I realize it's probably more psychological than physical.
Still, I'm not going to mess with a run I've been accustomed to for nearly twenty years, but I do wish, more often than not, that I had some way of tracking my run and how many miles I've done *exactly* while being outside. Sure, I can track the mileage by checking my phone before and after, but it would be nice to have a tracker on me without adding any psychological weight. I used to have a Polar watch that worked fine, but it died some time ago and I never bothered to get a replacement.
But finally I did.

With this one, I'm able to wear the watch without toting my phone along and it still carries all the features and tracking as if the phone were connected to any other tracking watch. While this watch is used for a number of cardio activities, I use it only for running. There are "pages" of exercises you can track, but for a quick run the default is set on the bottom left button--very nice to have, especially for me. Not sure if you can change the default on there to another exercise, but for me it's perfect and I haven't bothered looking up how to change it.
But curious to check out the full features, I ventured into the different pages (or screens) the watch has to offer. During my course, I found that the buttons were *very* stiff. This might be to prevent accidental presses during exercise, but I found that I had to press almost twice has hard as other electronic watches for the watch to recognize my press. But, from my uses so far, I've pressed it mostly to view all the screens when testing out all the features. When actually running, I do no more than a few presses before and after each run. The network had trouble activating itself in the beginning, but that's because I was fiddling with it outside. It kept trying to set itself numerous times when I actually ran outside, but I always dismissed it. Once, however, I was under the open sky I let it connect and it has had no problem or delay connecting ever since.

After every run I am able to sync it with the Epson app, as well as RunKeeper. People have complained about the Epson app but I find it neat and useful.

Overall, it's a great little watch that accurately records my runs and uploads them without the use of the phone during the workout. I'm able to review it speedily on my phone right after, and I love that I can now track my progress without the burden of added weight. It's pricey for sure, but considering I don't need my phone and my previous watch lasted me ten years, I'm sure this watch will be a great investment that will last me hopefully for another decade or so.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse Okay, so Razer has a reputation for making products that are of low quality or break prematurely. There may be some truth to that. The "back" button double and triple clicks. I am going to replace the switch.

There is an LED lighted scroll wheel which feels of quality. The sides are a hard smooth plastic. The rest the body is coated with a rubber-like material. There is a lighted Razer logo and I turned off all the LED's.

Even though there is a problem with my mouse I decided to keep it and fix the problem. I have to say that this is probably the most ergonomic, comfortable mouse I have ever used. It has a very high arch and is shaped for a palm grip. I personally don't know if it would be a good gaming mouse ever. The sides are VERY slippery and if you needed a lot of control I don't know if you would have it. Especially if you had to lift off the mouse to readjust, it may slip. In my opinion the Roccat XTD Kone is the best mouse I have ever used. It is very big and heavy and there are grooves for your thumb and outer fingers. It feels more sturdy.

The reason I gave it 3 stars instead of 4, the mouse is always a little warm to the touch and it seems to absorb heat from your hand and get hotter. The Roccat mouse is made from similar materials and always feels cool. I have heard that there are parts of the circuitry that generate more heat than normal. So in summary, I like it for general use. If I was gaming or doing something that requires precision such as graphic design I would use the Roccat Kone XTD.

Edit: follow up- I have owned this mouse now for 3 weeks and I have it next to the Roccat mouse. I should share that I have used the Razer almost exclusively and switched to the Roccat only when I needed to use forward and back buttons (they are hard to reach on Razer). I think the Razer is more comfortable to rest your hand on for long periods at a time. However, it just seems that I have better control of the right click, left click, and forward-back buttons. The DA causes your hand to form an arch, while your hand is more flat with the Roccat. I wonder if your index finger is in a stronger postion with the Roccat; it feels so.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Deathadder Infrared Gaming Mouse

text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops I've used much worse keyboards and mice, but I've also used much better. The keyboard is not bad, but speed typists would definitely prefer better. Because this is a full-size keyboard, be aware that you'll need ample space on your pull-out keyboard drawer. Some office desks have very narrow and shallow drawers. The mouse is okay too but feels a little cheap. However, this product was obviously not intended to be top-end.

My main criticism of this package is the somewhat confusing owner's manual. Every USB product I've used, particularly a kb or mouse, are plug-and-play. The manual gave instructions for "repairing' with the device, and it was unclear why you would need to issue the series of key commands in order to reconnect via USB on a PC. Perhaps this connection procedure applies only to other types of devices. After one brief failed attempt to connect (see next paragraph), the second try connected okay after I plugged in the USB dongle. I also unplugged/replugged the dongle and it worked again, without having to issue any of the "Esc + K" keypresses that the manual stated were necessary to repair the devices.

I suspect the range of this pairing is not very far. The first time I plugged the dongle in, neither the kb nor the mouse worked. I had to move both closer to the dongle before I got them to connect. The kb and mouse were only four feet from the dongle when I first installed them. After I finally got everything to connect at close range, I moved the kb and mouse back to the distance of four feet, and they continued to work. So I'm not sure of what distance would cause a disconnect.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops

text_fidelity_a:
Boogie Board LCD Writing Tablet - Sync for Note Taking with Bluetooth Feels Just Like Paper and Pencil I never new this existed and wish I would have found it sooner. I use it at work and love it. The sync is definately the way to go since it's the only one they make that you can save notes. The writing is light, but the screen is pressure sensitive so you just have to push harder or writing slower works too, but it shows up just fine for me at work. no complaints there. The real magic is when I sync my notes via Bluetooth to my phone/Evernote/Dropbox even, and I can immediately pull up the PDF at work and reference them. Plus if you have OCR in Adobe, Evernote, or another program that does the work, you can convert your notes PDF to a word document making it searchable and editable. I haven't found an OCR that's free yet, but it's not too expensive through adobe or Evernote. A small price to pay for the added functionality.

Only a few things would make this even better than it already is. It would be nice to be able to selectively delete parts of your notes, or erase mistakes (which hasn't been a real issue for me yet, I just cross out the mistake and rewrite it). And, you can edit notes on the computer with OCR, but it would be nice to be able to pull up old notes on the board to correct them or add to them on the board.

All in all I still love this thing and think it was well worth the money. Since I purchased it knowing it's capabilities and limitations there is no way to be disappointed with this. I love it!
text_fidelity_b: Boogie Board LCD Writing Tablet - Sync for Note Taking with Bluetooth Feels Just Like Paper and Pencil

I previously had 18" straps of a different, unknown brand and while they were good, they were just too long for some of the lower runs where there were fewer cables to tie up.

These are definitely the right length for just about everything the 18" can't handle. However, the quality isn't great - the hook part of the tab is fused onto the loop part of it, but on most they aren't perfectly aligned, and I broke three straps while cinching them down, all right at this juncture. Now it isn't a huge issue - to avoid straining the connection, you just pull on the main strap, not the end bit - but I really feel like that's something they should have gotten right. There just isn't that much to a cinch strap, after all.

Anyway, still three stars because only three broke and the rest were fine, and maybe I was pulling unreasonably hard on them in an attempt to corral the power cables, but maybe consider other brands and see if you have better luck there.

text_fidelity_a: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I just needed a cheap droid to take with me to places where I know I'll be sitting for a long time with nothing to do such as my kid's various school activities where they get to do all the stuff while the parents sit and wait.  If there is a wifi signal it will connect quickly.  At first I thought the battery didn't last very long until my oldest kid showed me what the little square at the bottom was for.  Now I get rid of all my trash and not let it build up wasting my battery.  I am surprised by how nice a droid this is and I only paid $39.00 for it.  I've paid much more for similar droids and they crashed and burned within a year or two.  I think this one will last a lot longer.  It comes with charging cord but it's too short to use if you're wanting to use the Kindle while it's charging, but it's nice to have as a spare cord. The screen has good clarity and nice touch response.  The sound quality is so-so but if I want to listen to music or watch a video I'll use earbuds. I really don't have any complaints about this Kindle Fire and I think it was $39.00 very well spent.  I just wish I had bought one a long time ago and saved myself several hundred dollars on the other droids that didn't last for very long or were too incredibly slow to even use.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO M-Series All-in-One 2.1 Immersive Sound Bar with 6 High-Performance Speakers, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Built in Subwoofers and Alexa Compatibility, M213ad-K8, 2023 Model I CHOSE this model over another because of the supposed built-in Alexa compatibility. You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO M-Series All-in-One 2.1 Immersive Sound Bar with 6 High-Performance Speakers, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Built in Subwoofers and Alexa Compatibility, M213ad-K8, 2023 Model

A few options that would have been a nice to have (but that don't bother me much) are

She was synced up and ready to go in just a few minutes. The mount went up easy and holds her phone with no problems. It recognizes her voice and responds fast to what she says. She can use it to change a song or call me when she needs some advice. It's easy to use and super awesome. Especially when she gets lost and she just asks Alexa to find directions to get from point A to point B. It's been super great so far. The only problem we have with this is the fact the only place you can put this is on a vent in your car. We don't like that at all because it gets super hot in the winter when she has the heater on. text_fidelity_a:
Shure SRH145m+ Portable Collapsible Headphones with Remote + Microphone Compatible with All Apple iOS Devices Update after 4 months

They have got more comfortable. I don't use them often so I don't think it's my ears that have got used to them I think the material has gotten softer with use and maybe the band has stretched out a bit.

I'll add to my review that while these are not hard to drive they are not easy to drive either. They are near the top of easy to drive. They are 32 ohms and sensitivity is 96db. What does that mean? I use these mostly with my computer that has a pretty good sound chip and I find that I have to have the computer sound (windows 7) and the music app (foobar 2000) volume all the way up to get these to where they open up and sound best. In general, they need to be a little louder than I would like to sound their best.

Sound wise I find myself punching up the bass a bit. They need a little bit more hit and a touch of bloom for things like the bass guitar and kik drum to sound about right. Not a lot, just a 3db boost from about 80 to 200hz. I also find they need a bit of a push at 10K and up to put a little more air around the instruments. With more listening, I'm not quite as thrilled with the sound as I was, but I still like them. Hours of listing do not leave me with ear fatigue and they do not punish poorly recorded music.

Update after a month:
These have not got more comfortable and I kinda wish I had returned them but for $32 it's not really worth it given I'd get charged $5 for the return. These hurt after a couple of hours and no amount of moving them around relieves it. The material is soft enough but I think it is too soft and packs down. Also clamping pressure is pretty high on my melon so now that I'm keeping them I may try to stretch them out a bit

================================================================

I am FUSSY about sound! I want natural neutral sound. That's what you get with these. The bass is natural, drums sound pretty good. Sibilance is there but not annoying. They are accurate without being clinical or fatiguing. They are musical without being over warm or polite. They do not punish poorly recorded music like some more HiFi headphones do. There is a nice amount of 'air' around the instruments but not much of a sound stage beyond that. They are a nice middle of the road set of headphone, not too bright, but bright enough, a good mid-range, pretty well-controlled bass without much bleed and some bass extension. They could use a touch more bloom to suit my tastes but what is there suits me fine. If I thought they were bass shy I would tell you.

I use a 15 band equalizer on my computer and I end up putting some EQ on most headphones I use, but I found with these I liked them best with no EQ. They do not go super loud with my phone. Loud enough for me, but not might be loud enough if you like your music really loud.They need a little volume to sound there best but that's pretty typical and I have had headphones that needed to be louder to sound their best.

They have one big problem. They are not very comfortable. I would not get these if wearing them all day at work is your thing of if comfort is really important to you because you get annoyed if they are not comfortable. In comparison, the Sennheiser HD 2.20 is WAY more comfortable. The foam is too thin and you almost feel like the plastic is pressed against your ears. They 2nd day they felt a little better. My ears getting used to them, or maybe the foam adapting to the shape of my ears or a little bit of both.The headband cushion is also really thin but did not bother me as much as the earpieces.

They have almost no isolation. My old open back Sennheiser 239 had more isolation. I'm also not a fan of how round that headband is but I guess they did that so they would fold up smaller? I don't know but I wish the fit a little closer to the head on the sides.

The cable is kind of weird in that the right and left cords are side by side like lamp cord and a little thicker than on other budget headphones.

Between my old Senn 239, and the Senn 2.20 and the Jabra Move (I think it was the Move) I like the sound of these Shure the best by far. If these cost $50 or even $60 I'd be really happy with these, at least for sound. For $30 dollars I'm REALLY happy with them.

I'd be tempted to knock a star off for comfort but for me, the sound is everything so the 5 stars are for the sound.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I knew right away that these would be my office headphones. I have a mechanical keyboard that I use at work, and the office I work in is semi-open. There's a *lot* of noise coming every-which-way. These are a much-needed accessory to my work productivity, as I'm easily distracted by things in my periphery, whether visually or auditory.

The presentation is great. The box is very high quality, reminiscent of the recent Samsung Galaxy device boxes. A smooth matte feel with gloss--weirdly pristine. The box slides out of the slipcover and you get the headphones already in the case. What I like is that they're folded, and there's even a little sheet underneath the phones that always reminds you how to put them back in. Also included is a 3.5mm cable in case you don't want to use Bluetooth, a charging cable, and an adapter. The case is nice, but as I keep mine at work I can't testify to its durability. There's a thin mesh net on the backside in case anyone needs to store one or two thin headphone accessory/-ies along. The accent colors are a nice light copper/rose gold color. I love that color; I'm glad it's getting more attention in recent years.

It didn't take long to charge the headphones, so they come with a little bit of juice. As soon as you turn them on, you get a soft beep along with a voice indicating they're turned on. Nice responsive feedback. Once I put them on I could hear the headphones working to drown out the sound; there was a thick veil of soundproofing that was draped over my ears as soon as the earpads touched them.

The first thing I did was listen to podcasts through the Pocket Casts app and .flac music through Poweramp v3. With podcasts, the difference was phenomenal. Listening to "Wait, wait... Don't tell me!" made me feel as though I were in the audience. The music was fantastic...until I tried on my other headphones which I use for music only.
I thought the bass might've been too strong with the Sony headphones, and I was right. After using even "cheaper" headphones like the Audio-Technica M50x, I could tell the Sony had too much bass. I'm not sure if that's partly because of the noise-canceling technology or what, but the bass can be toned down a bit, methinks.

I then proceeded to download the supplementary app to get the fullest suite of attributes the headphones can get. The app works well, and I didn't experience any hiccups while actually using the app. The only hiccup was when I was trying to download the update. It took *forever*. Almost an hour and it was just halfway through. I decided to bring them to work the next day and let the app sit there while updating. Thankfully, it remembers the progress, even though the app kept crashing during the update process.

There are some optimization tweaks in the app, some sound profiles to let you configure the noise cancelation level (yes, level; the noise cancelation is pure software; you can set it to drown out the most noise as possible or have no noise cancellation at all), and even a little snippet of what is currently playing through the headphones. A simple UI with all the features you need.

The first few days I used it I was active, and I kept noticing that my ears sometimes would pop depending on whether I sat down or arose quickly. Another weird thing is that when I take the headphones off, my ears sometimes need a minute or two to adjust. There's so much noise in the world! After taking the headphones off I can hear HVAC activity and my loud work neighbor who's otherwise not that loud.

I had some headphones with some touch controls before and always found them tacky. I used them once when I first got them and never again. But with these headphones, I'm always using the tap gesture to play/pause and the swipe gesture to raise or lower the volume. There are also swipe gestures to skip or go back a track, but since I never do that anyway I never use those gestures. You have to be careful with the tap; when it works, it works. But the whole surface isn't the active portion and you have to hit it right in the center. Sometimes I'm hitting my finger against my ears trying to find the spot and hurting myself in the process. I tested the gesture where you put your entire palm on the cup to turn off the noise canceling feature and let the mic allow incoming conversation, but not after the third try. I could hear the other people just fine, but I found the right hand over my ear felt awkward, and one person didn't realize I could even hear them. Putting your hand over your headphones isn't a gesture people immediately see as you paying attention to them.

The headphones are extremely lightweight and comfortable to use; I left them on for about two hours once before having to take them off. I actually was surprised with how light they were; when I got the Amazon box I didn't believe it was my headphones. It was much lighter than expected.

For my first noise-canceling headphones I'm pleased. The sound balance can be better (less bass), but they make for fantastic headphones to use at work. I wasn't sure what I was expecting with noise-canceling technology. I thought it would drown out all noises, but you still can hear the occasional mutter; it just won't be distinct.

Oh, forgot to mention the battery life. I charged it only once and have been using it for a week, at about an hour or two each day. Still going well. If you press the power button once it will tell you the battery level. AFter the initial update the voice indicator might give the wrong battery level (it did for me), but give it about ten or fifteen minutes to adjust and it will go back to normal.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version)

Sony X800H 55-inch TV: 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with HDR and Alexa Compatibility - 2020 Model Background: I spec and integrate the highest resolution LCD’s produced in aerospace defense applications. LCD image performance is measured in hundreds of dimensions and environments. Sony is not a player in that space.

For home, I’ve been SID show and showroom shopping LCD, OLEDs, etc image quality for years. This year, I’m replacing a comparably sized exercise room 1080p LCD set. Sony has always been, to my eye, a superb comparative model and a $100 or so more than other competitors. Is the premium worth it?

This Sony X800H is an eye grabber across the showroom and on close inspection. It’s a phenomenal picture. Sony’s proprietary LCD foundries are unique in the industry. The Sony LCD foundry produces a distinctive LCD that is worth the premium price to the discerning.

Performance-wise, Sony reduced the native refresh rate to 60hz from 120hz last year. That’s quite practical as it will be some years before >60fps cameras are widely available at native 120fps. No matter, the 60hz to 120hz refresh is not discernible to the eye. The X800H imaging software can be seen to take care of latency artifacts at factory default settings … no viewing distance ghosting, inverse ghosting, blur or pulse-width modulation.

There is a comment regarding darkness, edge lighting, and illumination issues. The X800H is both edge and background light as best as I can discern without tearing it apart. It's uniform lighting no matter. Sony has always been the master of the best 'optical black' pixel to enrich the color pixel perception. The X800H is loaded with image quality controls. Image software quality defaults arrived set at factory default. It was perfect out of the box. Don't adjust anything. I rarely futz with default settings. No one should have to. The vast majority of image problems are video source input. Change the channel first and compare the image.

An old school key attribute is viewing angles … how many degrees left/right and horizontal/vertical are necessary to degrade the image. The viewing angles here are excellent. Viewing angles are a peek into the remarkable quality of Sony’s proprietary LCD foundry.

Sony’s software, firmware, Smart integration, and image processors are likewise Sony proprietary. Sony names these features like everyone else. Feature comparisons are mostly apparent in year over year Sony tech evolution.

Of course, the real story is in the final image quality. The X800H is one excellent viewing experience.

Better than advertised. Better than expected. In this size, the X800H is the benchmark, IMHO.
text_fidelity_b: Sony X800H 55-inch TV: 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with HDR and Alexa Compatibility - 2020 Model

2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters Likes.

Well made.
Long cord. The long cord is very important.

Setup.

I used the long cord to place it on the floor, next to my patio door.
I then set my TV to auto scan.
It gave me many more stations than my non amplified leaf antennae pulled in.
Every station was crystal clear.
However, that was not a convenient permanent location, so I then placed it behind the TV.
It was important to first place it in the best possible area, in my case against the patio door to identify all possible stations.

Issues.

After auto scan identified all possible stations, I moved the antenna to behind my entertainment center. I lost half the stations. But, the TV showed those station numbers, it just couldn't pull them in. I then placed it flat on top of the entertainment center. It improved the reception. I then slid it partially inside my TV wall mount hardware, flat against the wall. It gave me excellent reception on all identified stations.

My advice.

Take advantage of the long cord, move it next to a window even if it won't be left there. You can then place the antenna in more convenient locations, trying to get back to as many identified stations as possible.
text_fidelity_b: 2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EOS Rebel T3i Digital SLR Camera with EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Lens (discontinued by manufacturer) **Please note that this review was written by a novice photographer.
I have been asking my husband for a camera for years. You know how it is....the entire time he is taking pictures with his Nikon D80 (he fancies himself a fantastic photographer...and he is), I am constantly in his ear telling how what I see and envision would make a better picture. I also tell him how he should take a picture of something that I believe will make him the next Ansel Adams. And I complete the photo shoot with, "if only I had really good camera, I would"..... Well, I guess he was tired of hearing it, and decided to buy me this camera (for Christmas thru Amazon) if for no other reason than to shut me up. I guess it was his way of putting "his" money where "my" mouth is, and I was delighted.

Now what is there to like about this camera.
-This camera is user friendly and great for a beginner photographer or at least one that is ready to move from a camera like a Nikon CoolPix. It is perfect for still shots and video (HD). It is easy to select a setting (portrait, action, etc), point and shoot. It focuses automatically (press halfway) and can be manually adjusted (tight or far away photos). There is a menu that allows you to edit and even make images, black and white. **Please note that this is the one feature that no matter how much I read the manual, I can't quite get it to do what I would like. I can edit a picture, change it to black & white, and even use the zoom tool, but when I attempt to save it, it won't. That is a feature that I will have to continue to fool with. And if anyone can help me, I would appreciate it.
-You can manipulate the viewing screen...it flips out and turns (for use while recording video) so that you can view it. Or you can swivel, flip and turn the screen around and collapse it against the body of the camera. This allows you to see or view the pictures you are taking or have taken.
- This camera takes crisp/clear photos. They are amazingly clear.
-This camera has a continuously shoot feature/function. It is great for my son's wrestling matches.
-This camera has an automatic flash that is useful if you aren't sure about the lighting.
-This camera is light (weight wise) enough to carry around for a long period of time (your hand won't get tired), but it also comes with a comfortable and adjustable neck strap. There are also cords that come with the camera so that you can use with the computer or TV.
-The battery life is decent. I assume that it also depends on how many videos you do versus still shots. However, I have done both and found and didn't have a problem. This camera also comes with a convenient battery charger.
Overall, I love my new Canon Rebel T3i and look forward to (a) learning everything about it that I can and (2) taking tons of fantastic pictures for years to come.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EOS Rebel T3i Digital SLR Camera with EF-S 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 IS Lens (discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model) I purchased this at the end of July 2014 along with:

[[ASIN:B00E5NOXM4 Google Nexus 7 2013 Case - Poetic Google Nexus 7 2013 Case [Slimline Series] - [Lightweight] [Ultra-slim] PU Leather Slim-Fit Trifold Cover Stand Folio Case for Google Nexus 7 2nd Gen 2013 Black (3 Year Manufacturer Warranty From Poetic)]]

[[ASIN:B008MOHLVC Stylus, amPen® Hybrid Stylus (Black) for Apple iPad Air/iPad 2/iPad Mini, Apple iPhone 6 (4.7)/6 Plus (5.5)/5/5s/5c/4s, Nexus 5/7, Galaxy Tab 4/3/2, Galaxy S5/S4, HTC One M8/M7 (Interchangeable Hybrid Tip Feature)]].

I also ordered the [[ASIN:1937842282 Google Nexus 7 (Android 4.4 KitKat Edition)]] book as a compliment to this purchase.

I waited almost six months to write this review because I wanted to "cool off" from my installation experience that would have caused me to rate this 3 stars. I am also now able to fairly assess this tablet after a few months' use.

I wanted a highly-rated unrestricted (open) tablet that provided great graphics and sufficient screen space. I purchased this to use on a Wi-Fi network only for when I didn't want to boot up my laptop to check mail or see a movie, etc. I also did not want an Apple tablet because my boyfriend has an iPad 3 and the Apple products have restrictions. I also was not impressed with the graphics on his iPad. I was considering a Kindle Fire HD 7" but that tablet was too restrictive as well and was geared to Amazon junkies. I am an Amazon junkie but I also do not like restrictions on products I purchase. During my July 2014 research, I discovered that the Nexus 7 tablet was the highest rated Android next to those more restrictive tablets.

After I received the Nexus, I wondered if I had made the right decision. First, I was surprised that this came with no documentation (other than the business card sized diagram of where all the ports were and a warranty and safety agreement in both English and French). The documentation didn't even say how long I needed to charge the unit. I charged it overnight and then had immense trouble getting this connected.

The router I was connecting to has MAC filtering enabled so I needed the MAC address. However, I couldn't get the MAC address without setting up the device. Also, I couldn't set it up because I couldn't get the MAC address. I could have fussed with the router and turned off MAC filtering/security temporarily but I had to get to work in the morning right after the unit completed charging. I then tried connecting via three other networks (my library for one, my work another, and another Wi-Fi connection). It still would not connect. Because I didn't want to wait until I got home 12 hours later to fuss with my router I wound up asking a tech support person where I work. He connected me via his personal MiFi mobile hotspot.

Apparently, Google Nexus only connects to certain networks if the first time setup has not been done. I tried several open networks. My co-worker's MiFi mobile network connection, although I suspect mine would have connected had I temporarily removed the security on my router, was the only one that would allow me to run the automatic setup so that I could connect. After setup was performed, I was able to get the MAC address from the settings "about" tab. I was also able to connect to the three other networks I tried previously and after inputting the MAC address, I could also connect to my router. It was apparently the initial setup process that prevented the connection.

This Google Nexus would have gotten five stars if they enhanced the user experience by:
1 - Providing a MAC address either on the unit or on a piece of paper for those that have MAC filtering enabled.
2 - Providing a documentation pamphlet with the unit that:
* Tells the user how long they need to charge the unit the first time.
* Explains to the user that setup cannot be run on all networks and sometimes they will get an error message. Therefore, they might say something like "using your own network is advisable" or provide an explanation of why certain networks (including totally open ones that allow all connections) would not work. Perhaps there is some sort of technical protocol that is not available on all networks; I have no idea.

Other than the above, I absolutely love my Google Nexus. I've been using this for almost 6 months and it has met my every expectation. It charges in less than four hours; lasts about 3 hours if I'm constantly using it; lasts about 3-4 days when I'm using it for about 10 minutes daily. I've used this for email, movies, web surfing, pictures, etc. App availability is unending (Kindle, LinkedIn, Battery Doctor, etc., etc.) I tested the screen image next to my co-workers Kindle Fire HD 7" and there is no discernible difference in quality or resolution. Images and movies on this device are superb. If I attach my [[ASIN:B00N4SIIFY APLWL USB 2.0 A to Micro B Cable 6FT-TPE jacket-Blue]] to my laptop, I can both charge the unit and also access files on it from my laptop such as the photos located under Nexus 7\Internal storage\DCIM\Camera directory (that's Computer\Nexus 7\Internal storage\DCIM\Camera in Explorer).

Overall this is a quality tablet that did not disappoint me once I got past the initial installation and lack of documentation headache. In the comments section of my review, I put links to Google documentation I found helpful as well as to the 2014 review I used for my research.

UPDATE Jan 6, 2015 - Right after I wrote this review I had a problem where my Nexus was shutting down automatically and every time I went to use it I had to power it back up. After doing an Internet search I was able to fix this by going to the Play Store app on the Nexus, then selecting "My Apps" and accepting all install updates. There were a few updates that had not installed and this was playing havoc with my system. After I did this, the Nexus remained powered up and has been working fine the last several days.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS Overall, this is a very nice golf GPS for the price. I was a little worried about it being too complicated to use, but the manual explains all the features in reasonably good detail. I found it helpful to keep the manual with me the first couple of times I used it on the course to refer to, but after a few outings I felt comfortable using it.

I had an initial problem with the battery life in that it quit on me after about an hour of use. After leaving it in the charging cradle overnight, the next time it maintained its charge for a full afternoon's use. I've used it (and recharged it) several times since then and have had no problems, so it seems the first time was just a momentary glitch (or perhaps I didn't seat the charging cable firmly enough).

I very much like that it does not require a subscription to use, nor does it need to be tethered to a PC for the initial setup. It has a pretty extensive database of courses (Izzo says on their website that they cover 90% of the courses in the US). You can use their website to look up a course to see if it is included in the database.

Sat acquisition times is quick - took only a few minutes to get a lock and find my course the first time I used it. Acquisition time was even faster on subsequent uses. It uses a SiRF Star III receiver.

The display is clear even in sunlight, but it is a bit small for me. I don't usually have my reading glasses with me when I'm outdoors, so seeing the distance numbers took quite a bit of squinting. Granted, if you don't have aging eyes you won't find that to be a problem, but it would have been nice to have a larger display.

I also didn't find it all that comfortable to wear. It is lightweight and not too thick, but the strap was not very comfortable. Plus the greenish/yellow accent color (found on the inside of the strap and the sides of the unit) didn't appeal to me much - rather garish looking to my eye.

The warranty is only 90 days, which I think is too short given the price -- a year would be more appropriate.

But those are minor quibbles. Overall, the functionality is great - quick to acquire sats, accurate distances and straightforward to use. Considering the price of other brands, such as Garmin, this is a great value. Definitely should be on the short list if you're shopping for a golf GPS.

[As an aside, it's a real bear to the product out of the clamshell packaging. I didn't' factor that into the rating, but set aside some time to wrestle it out of the plastic jail it comes in should you buy one.]
text_fidelity_b: Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS

text_fidelity_a:
TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.
text_fidelity_b: TV Antenna - 1byone Amplified 50 Mile HDTV Digital Antenna Powerful Amplifier Signal Booster for All TV 4K UHF VHF 1080P Local Channels with 20ft Coaxial Cable

text_fidelity_a:
eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee I contacted Eufy after the battery died after 4 weeks. Took them 2 days to send me an autobot emailed response to which I responded that I wanted a live person to email me. Another 2 days, and a person asked me to send a screen shot of the battery settings. REALLY??? So I did that which my battery settings were for optimized battery life. Another 2 days and still no answer. There was an option on the bottom of their email to escalate the case to management if I was not happy with the response, and that they would get back to me within 24 hours. So I clicked it, and explained how I was not getting a response. But guess what? I never got a response. So five days later, I decided to return this because I'm still in the return window. Maybe I had a defective unit. We have had a very mild winter, so I cannot imagine that the weather would make a supposed four-month battery charge only last for four weeks. Plus, there isn't much motion going on to drain the battery either. Sometimes, 3 or 4 days go by with no motion. The most number of times it has detected motion in one day is four times. So it's not like the battery is getting drained from the camera being triggered 10 times a day. I'm going to try one more time, and watch the battery life to see how quickly it drains before the return window closes.

**** Update **** The replacement camera will have a battery life of approximately 6 or 7 weeks, judging by the amount of battery used thus far. Since the return window is just 4 weeks, I have returned this camera again and will not try another one. 6-7 weeks battery life is better than 4 weeks, for sure. But still disappointing because Eufy advertises a 4 month battery life. I would have been willing to try to Eufy 2 Pro that has a 365-day battery life (figuring it probably really only has a 6 month battery life). But this would mean purchasing a home base. Also, the location of the camera does not get any direct sunlight, so even a solar panel would not have helped. If you are looking for just one camera that is wireless, and you aren't interested in having to take it down every month or two for recharging, this is not the camera for you. Their customer support contacted me the day after I wrote my first review. (I couldn't get any support previously through their normal channels.)
text_fidelity_b: eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers Our daughters' charter school uses Kindle readers for their textbooks so we bought them each one Sept. 2011. Both Kindles are still working really well, and we're pleased with their durability. Because of the daily use during the week, they need to charge them every couple of days. But that is a simple matter to take care of. Once they've finished their homework they plug them in, then in the morning unplug before we head off for school. I have noticed that due to the frequent use, the numbers & letters have worn off of most of the keys. That could be a bit of an issue but the girls have memorized which key is for which letter or number.

I like how there's little to no glare in the sun, the Kindle is easier to read than other readers or a tablet. Because of the ease in obtaining books, especially many of the Classics for free, the Kindle has increased our daughters' love of reading even more. My one small complaint with the charger is that the white plastic cover on the cord is splitting near the end pieces. I've considered contacting Amazon regarding that because it's obvious that it's due to a defect. If I do, I'll update here.

Overall, we're very happy with Kindle and plan at some point to buy more readers for the rest of the family.

text_fidelity_a:
Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green) I've been testing this speaker system with my 10" Samsung Galaxy Tab2 tablet which had no problems connecting to the speakers with and without the app from the Android store.

Appearance:
Their product description calls this 'fun, trendy and modern'. But to be honest this looks, to me, like an appliance that fell out of my grandmother's 1950's black, white and chrome art-deco kitchen. It's not unpleasant looking but I wouldn't call it modern. When I saw images of the system online I had hopes that the neon green ring around the face would light up. Sadly it doesn't. The handle is also fixed in place and doesn't retract or collapse into the body. It would have been a nice idea so you could stack or store this more easily.

Sound:
It doesn't sound bad. Especially for being just two 15 watt wide range speakers in a ported (holes to help the bass sound better) enclosure. The bass is a little flat and the high end sounds a little... hollow but it is a lot better than the speakers built into my tablet. I've tried a variety of music; jazz, pop, classical, rock, punk and everything sounded quite good. I found I had to use both the tablet's volume control as well as the speaker systems volume controls to get real volume out of the system. They operate independently of each other.

Drawbacks:
I don't normally comment on price with items received from the Vine program but at the time I'm writing this review Amazon is currently selling this item for over two hundred dollars. Maybe the Bluetooth equipment is expensive but to me that's a LOT for just two speakers in a box. I didn't pay that much for my four speaker bookshelf system or the subwoofer equipped speaker system connected to my desktop PC. Both of which have far superior sound quality.

The battery indicator light only seems to light up when the system is charging. I charged this a week ago and used it for several hours at a time but I have no idea how much charge is left in the battery.

The biggest problem I had with this speaker system was when doing anything other than playing music. I thought it would be fun to add big sound to the games I enjoy on my tablet but there's a distinct lag between doing anything and when the speaker plays the sound. I noticed it most of all in my favorite billiards simulator. You would strike a ball...and then hear it happen, even system sounds such as keyboard typing noises, a 'blip' when selecting things played a noticeable time after they happened.

The App:
I won't say much about the app here. It's completely unnecessary to operate this system with your Android device. It's just poor quality programming that appears to have been slapped together at the last minute. It also doesn't match the documentation and features such as Bass Boost which are in the instructions but don't exist in the app.

Speaking of the documentation. I opened the box and found a large booklet and for one, brief, moment I thought this item was fully documented in depth and detail... then I opened the instructions and found there's twelve pages of English instructions which are poorly written and lacking in detail. The rest of the book is comprised of numerous other languages each getting their own few pages. Ah well. Turn it on, turn it up. Enjoy the music.
text_fidelity_b: Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green)

Better than expected. Excellent value for money. One wonders how it can be made at the price.

There was nothing wrong except the way the stand splits open at the bottom. There are these little plastic nubs that hold it in position kind of like gears and they're like 1mm high and made of cheap plastic. They are visibly scuffed or fused funny and I have opened it maybe 3 or 4 times. They wont last. Also most of the adjustments for the back part that holds the tablet up, do not sit flush with the back of the tablet. It's just kind of a flawed product design. I feel like I'm being harsh but it's true.

My advice would be to get something else for a couple bucks more. There's an entire category for laptop stands on amazon and there are tablet stands within it. There are a lot of happy customers of this product so I may have just gotten one that slipped passed quality control. Good luck guys.

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android The WEWATCH V30 Portable Projector is a good 1080p projector for its size. I watched some movies with the screen setup to 80-90 inches and the picture looked very good in a dark room. It's important to watch this projector in low ambient lighting due to its low ANSI lumens, as bright light will wash out the picture.

The size of the projector is not as small as the pictures make it seem. Though it is not advertised as a pico projector, I expected it to be smaller. With that said, the projector is not so large that it would be hard to transport or store when not in use.

Unfortunately, I was not able to get the Wi-Fi feature to work with my Iphone. This is not a dealbreaker for me, as I plugged a Roku stick into the HDMI port and the system worked well.

I was surprised by how good the native speakers sound. I found watching movies enjoyable and voices were easy to hear. There are adjustments for the bass and treble levels in the menus. The unit has a headphone jack in the rear which makes hooking up an external speaker set up a breeze.

The fan on the unit is very quiet and is not distracting while it is in use.

While I really like this projector, there is a large downside. The lack of keystone correction is a huge oversight. Placing this projector without keystone adjustment means the projector has to be directly in line with the viewing area making it necessary to use a tripod in most instances. Having to bring a tripod along, makes the unit less portable.

Overall, this is a small projector with a great picture, as long as you can place it in the perfect location without much ambient lighting. If WEWATCH added keystone correction and refined the mirroring feature, this would be a 5 star projector.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android

text_fidelity_a: Sanus Adjustable Height Speaker Stand - Extends 28" to 38" - Holds Satellite & Small Bookshelf Speakers (i.e. Bose, Harmon Kardon, Polk, JBL, KEF, Klipsch, Sony and Others) - Set of 2 - Model: HTBS First step per instructions is to detach 10 felt pads, one at a time, from the paper backing and place them on the 10 legs (5 each) on the bottom of the 2 heavy metal base pieces. What a pain as these fiddly little felt pads don't detach easily from the backing. And are so small they are hard to position on the legs just right. Black on black. Hard to see. And why 5 when 3 bigger ones would do it? I have bought desktop computers and other items with the rubber feet already installed. Why not these? What would it cost the manufacturer? Peanuts. Aluminum pipes screw together fine but when the speakers are installed, with the base oriented as per instructions, whole thing pitches forward. Solution: orient the bases in the opposite direction and the balance is better. Better not perfect. To get a straight up balanced posture, the bases will have to be shimmed in front. Not the end of the world but still. Tip: during assembly, ignore instructions and attach speakers to the upper pipe alone and then insert the upper pipe into the lower pipe and tighten down the friction-fit as needed. Much easier than wrangling the whole assembly with heavy base attached. And I wonder if this system will hold the speakers solidly to permit the full bass sound to be projected. Won't these flimsy pipes allow the speaker to vibrate and so loose sound energy projection? Much better would be mounting the Polks on the wall (for resonance) but this was not an option.

I will be honest: I reluctantly purchased this device. I've been using trackballs since around 1997 because my original computer space didn't really accommodate a standard mouse, and I really haven't gone back to mice. The corded Logitech Trackman has been my favored trackball for years. My cat chewed through the cord, and it eventually stopped working right, so I had to upgrade. Having a wireless trackball has always seemed rather redundant to me; why would you need cordless when you never move it? Well, it's actually quite nice to not fiddle with the cord! I didn't realize how annoying having a tether is until you no longer have it...

At any rate, this trackball is remarkably accurate (I play several games and work with large spread sheets,) and a snap to install. In short, a reluctant customer is very satisfied!
